### Jones County

- **Type:** County
- **Recorded status:** ⚪ Replaced

The county's own account (reported by The Jones County News, a local outlet, citing county officials) states commissioners 'initially approved a moratorium on data centers in October of 2025' to allow further research before adopting permanent zoning language; that moratorium/work-session period concluded with the unanimous adoption of a permanent M-2 Data Center text amendment at a called meeting on January 16, 2026.
- **Normalized date:** `2025-10` (month_only)
- **Duration:** The October 2025 moratorium/work-session period ran until the Board adopted a permanent text amendment (rather than a further dated moratorium) at a called meeting on January 16, 2026, unanimously (5-0).
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `ga-jones-county-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Jones County M-2 Data Center Ordinance (comprehensive land use plan / land use amendment adding data centers as a conditional use in M-2 industrial zoning), adopted unanimously (5-0) at a called Board of Commissioners meeting on January 16, 2026, replacing the rescinded September 2025 zoning amendments and the intervening October 2025 moratorium.
- **What prompted it:** Legal notice defects under Georgia zoning procedure law and project-pressure concerns
- **Affected projects:** Developer withdrew 600-plus-acre rezoning proposal after public opposition
- **Detailed status:** Replaced, as of 2026-09-23. The January 16, 2026 M-2 Data Center Ordinance (conditional use in M-2 industrial zoning, with 200-foot setbacks, 400-foot setbacks for noise-generating buildings, up to 200-foot buffers, 55/45 dB noise limits, and closed-loop cooling requirements) remains in force but is under active legal challenge: 17 Jones County residents filed a declaratory-judgment lawsuit in February 2026 seeking to void the ordinance on due-process and Georgia Zoning Procedures Law grounds; the county filed a motion to dismiss in March 2026, and as of a Jones County Development Authority meeting reported by The Jones County News, the judge had not yet set a hearing on that motion, with the attorney estimating a 2027 timeline. The litigation has effectively frozen marketing of the underlying Griswoldville Industrial Park site.
- **Outcome:** Reset to re-adopt defensible zoning controls

An extension of the moratorium between those dates has not been established.

- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ga-monroe-county-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution on Data Center Moratorium prepared by Brandon Bowen of Jenkins, Bowen & Walker, P.C., approved 4-1 on 2025-12-16, superseded by a permanent ordinance amending the Monroe County Unified Development Ordinance (restricting data centers to Special Use in M-1 zoning; adding setback, buffer, generator, lighting, sound, and utility standards), posted by the county as agenda item '04-07-26 C. Data Center Ordinance Amendment' and, per a county Facebook post, unanimously approved by the Board of Commissioners on April 7, 2026.
- **What prompted it:** Community backlash to hyperscale proposals (Forsyth Technology Campus) and prior approvals
- **Affected projects:** A ~950-acre rezoning off Rumble Road for a data center was approved in November 2024, and Google purchased the property for $42 million in September 2025 for a potential development; because that project had not yet been constructed, county officials stated the new April 7, 2026 UDO standards would apply to it as well as to future projects. The Forsyth Technology Campus concept (now annexed into the City of Forsyth) is a separate matter reported in the same period.
- **Detailed status:** Replaced, as of 2026-09-23. After the March 3, 2026 meeting tabled the proposed amendment for revision (adding a larger 500-foot buffer with 100 feet of natural growth, a well-water ban, and Tier 4 generator requirements), the Monroe County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved the revised Unified Development Ordinance amendment on April 7, 2026, restricting data centers to Special Use in M-1 zoning countywide with detailed setback, buffer, noise, lighting, and utility standards. No further extension, repeal, or replacement of that ordinance was located as of 2026-09-23.
- **Outcome:** County working on UDO amendments addressing data centers (noise, water, buffers, etc.) per Chairman Gibbs comments at 2025-12-16 meeting
